name: Anuj Kapoor

thesis.text: I go where technology is rewriting economics and markets,

strap: Right now that means making a forest as legible to markets as a bond, threading solar energy systems with a distributed platform, putting Himalayan supply chains on digital rails from loom to London, and building digital intelligence that lets a small team move at the scale of an institution. Trained as a banker and technology strategist, wired as a founder, and drawn into policy and advisory because the future needs better rules, I spend half my time thinking ten years ahead and the other half building towards it.
workNote: Open to partnerships built on shared value.

tile.title: About me
tile.teaser: Venture and product builder, asking one question for twenty years.

panel.title: How human systems and economics change when technology arrives

blocks.text: One question has run through my career: how do people and economies evolve when new technology arrives?

I trained in classical economics and business, then went to the London School of Economics for an MSc, studying how new media and information systems, at the dawn of social media, were shaping the evolution of social and economic systems. I then spent eight years inside the machinery of capital, structuring cross-asset derivatives at Citigroup and investments at EFG Private Bank.

By 2011–12 a new field was emerging: decentralised systems and distributed economics, driven by Satoshi Nakamoto's 2008 paper. Here was an information system redesigning money, trust and institutions. I left banking in 2012 to follow it and see it work in the real world.

Since then the pattern has repeated. Find the shift early, learn its economics, technology and incentives properly, then put it to work: in a Himalayan village, at a London market stall, in a gamified augmented-reality world, in natural assets, inside an AI system and in policy.
Deeply multidisciplinary: I enjoy going deep enough into a new field to build something that really works, then connecting it to everything else I know.

items.title: GreenPeople.earth · Founder Director
items.text: Data, data intelligence and fintech for environmental markets. Built Green Intelligence, an AI project-data environment that maps renewable, nature-based carbon and environmental projects against markets, regulations and registries.

items.title: Five Benches · Founder Director
items.text: Supply chains for provenance-rich goods from the lower Himalayas, built with villages and women's self-help groups: production systems, digital identity, e-commerce, logistics and direct sales in London and Europe. Through Himalayan People I gave Chamba Chukh, a chilli preserve made by a remote community of chilli growers and women's self-help groups, its digital identity and built its supply chain from the villages to export and e-commerce markets.

items.title: Chamba Chukh, from a remote valley to the world map
items.text: Working with chilli growers and women's self-help groups in a remote Himalayan community, I created the digital identity for their community product, Chamba Chukh, and launched it on the web. I built the whole supply chain from the villages to export and e-commerce markets, putting it on the global map of provenance-rich chilli products. It drew attention from national news channels and media, and the state government later put it forward for Geographical Indication (GI) certification.

blocks.text: Born in Shimla, in the Himalayan hills, into a family of doctors, engineers and lawyers. Educated in cities around the world.

items.label: Mother
items.title: Law
items.text: Educated in law, a retired judge and former Secretary of the Himachal Pradesh Legal Aid Board. She now serves on ethics boards and committees at academic institutions in the state.

items.label: Brother
items.title: Writing & enterprise
items.text: Published writer and poet, former market researcher and creative director. Co-founder of Five Benches, the enterprise helping Himalayan makers create market-ready products.

blocks.text: My partner is a software consultant, and we live between London and Shimla.

Several of my creative ventures began by solving small problems for the people around me. Himalayan People started as a way to connect communities near where I was born to digital markets. Festival People is a game I designed so my family could celebrate festivals together from wherever we were. Green Intelligence came from noticing that hardworking small enterprises and makers in rural communities struggled to pitch their work to funders and grant makers. It now does that for them, leaving them free to get on with their real work, which is in atoms, not digits.

blocks.text: How I engage

I work on conventional consulting and advisory terms, and I'm especially drawn to partnerships, equity or shared-upside arrangements and long-term collaborations, where reward follows the value we create together.
If you're building something worthwhile and would like to work together, I'd be glad to hear from you.
